definition: Geographical mobility is the extent to which a person’s life involves movement between places, such as longer-distance commuting or relocating for work, study, marriage, or other long-term living arrangements. In this context, greater geographical mobility means greater exposure to different local environments and variation across places over time.

reasons: The packet discusses mobility in relation to dialect/language variation (e.g., exposure to dialectal variation and dialect change), but the definition broadens this to “different local environments” and “variation across places” in a general, non-linguistic sense that is not explicitly supported by the packet.

The packet gives examples of mobility patterns (longer-distance commuting; easier relocation for work, study or marriage), but it does not explicitly define geographical mobility as “the extent to which a person’s life involves movement between places” as a general conceptual definition.

The packet frames the idea through a proposed metric (Linguistic Mobility Index) and linguistic exposure; it does not support the definition’s framing of geographical mobility in general life terms beyond the linguistic/biographical context.
